name: Alqubba
description: A star 145 parsecs away, 39 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 94160: radius 38.553 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 601.57 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.065) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 94160: effective temperature 4607 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.066)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 94160: distance 145.349 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.036), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 145 parsecs away, 39 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 602 times the Sun's luminosity at 4,607 K, so 38.553 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 94160: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Beta Coronae Australis
quotes.card: Beta Coronae Australis, also named Alqubba, is a solitary star located in the southern constellation Corona Australis.
quotes.introduction: Its Bayer designation is Latinized from β Coronae Australis, and abbreviated Beta CrA or β CrA.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 6717964750922730624 (quality A), from 2006AstL...32..759G; Gaia DR3 measures none
